# Quick Study Guide: 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle

> "MongoDB does not have a dedicated command to create a database ahead of time. Switching to a database name that doesn't exist yet (with the use statement) selects it, but the database is only actually created once you insert data into a collection within it. The use statement switches the current database context for all subsequent commands in the session. db.dropDatabase() permanently deletes the currently selected database, including all of its collections and documents. This action cannot be undone."

## 1. Topic Executive Overview

This advanced systems revision sheet distills the high-yield architectural invariants of **1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle**, covering wire protocol commands, WiredTiger storage behavior, B-tree index impact, and edge-case failure modes.

## 1.1 Database Context Switching & Creation (use <databaseName>)

> "MongoDB does not have a dedicated command to create a database ahead of time. Switching to a database name that doesn't exist yet (with the use statement) selects it, but the database is only actually created once you insert data into a collection within it. The use statement switches the current database context for all subsequent commands in the session."

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax (`use <databaseName>`) — Dynamic In-Memory Selection & Active Session Pointer.** In `mongosh`, `use <databaseName>` rebinds the session-scoped `db` proxy object to `<databaseName>` in `O(1)` client time. Every subsequent operation invoked on `db.<collection>` serializes `<databaseName>.<collection>` as the full namespace (`ns`) inside `OP_MSG` wire frames.
- **L-3.2 Execution Behavior — Zero Pre-Allocation & First-Write Disk Materialization.** MongoDB intentionally omits a standalone `CREATE DATABASE` wire command. Until a mutating command (`insert`, `create`, or `update` with `upsert: true`) executes against the namespace, `_mdb_catalog.wt` contains zero entries for `<databaseName>`. Upon the initial write, WiredTiger atomically registers the database namespace, allocates `collection-*.wt`, and initializes the mandatory `_id_` B-tree index (`index-*.wt`).

```javascript
// 1. Volatile client-side lexical binding (Zero server RPC or disk I/O)
use schoolDB
// Internal shell binding: db -> Mongo.getDB("schoolDB")
// At this stage, { listDatabases: 1 } (show dbs) excludes "schoolDB".

// 2. First-write storage engine materialization
db.students.insertOne({ name: "Aditi", age: 18, grade: 8 });
// Server executes OP_MSG { insert: "students", $db: "schoolDB", documents: [...] }
// WiredTiger commits _mdb_catalog.wt entry + collection-*.wt + index-*.wt (_id_).
```

| Execution Stage | Shell / Wire Action | `_mdb_catalog.wt` State | WiredTiger `.wt` Files Allocated |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pre-Selection | Default session (`test`) | Unmodified | None |
| `use schoolDB` | Client lexical rebind (`O(1)`) | Zero entries for `schoolDB` | `0` files (volatile pointer only) |
| `insertOne({...})` | `OP_MSG` `{ insert: "students" }` | Registers `schoolDB.students` | `collection-*.wt` + `index-*.wt` (`_id_`) |

## 1.2 Database Catalog Inspection (show dbs)

> "show dbs lists all databases on the MongoDB server that contain at least one collection, along with their size on disk. Databases that have only been selected with use (without any data written to them) will not appear here."

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax (`show dbs`) — Server-Wide Inventory & `sizeOnDisk` Reporting.** The `show dbs` shell helper wraps `db.adminCommand({ listDatabases: 1 })`, which returns `{ databases: [ { name, sizeOnDisk, empty }, ... ], totalSize, totalSizeMb, ok: 1 }`. The shell formats `sizeOnDisk` into gigabytes.
- **L-3.2 Visibility Rules — Unwritten Namespace Exclusion & Internal System Databases.** Because `_mdb_catalog.wt` only records materialized namespaces, unpopulated `use` bindings never appear in `listDatabases`. Conversely, `admin` (RBAC credentials & cluster roles), `config` (shard chunk maps & logical session tables), and `local` (instance startup log & replication `oplog.rs`) contain internal collections and are always visible.

```javascript
// 1. Shell helper inspection
show dbs
// admin      0.000GB
// config     0.000GB
// local      0.000GB
// schoolDB   0.000GB

// 2. Equivalent underlying wire command executed by mongosh
db.adminCommand({ listDatabases: 1 });
// Returns: { databases: [ { name: "admin", sizeOnDisk: 40960, empty: false }, ... ], ok: 1 }
```

| Namespace | Storage Catalog Status | Core Internal Collections | Replicated Across Replica Set? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `admin` | Persisted in `_mdb_catalog.wt` | `system.users`, `system.roles`, `system.version` | Yes |
| `config` | Persisted in `_mdb_catalog.wt` | `system.sessions`, `shards`, `chunks` | Yes |
| `local` | Persisted in `_mdb_catalog.wt` | `startup_log`, `oplog.rs`, `replset.minvalid` | **No** (strictly node-local) |
| `schoolDB` | Persisted after first write | User collections (`students`, etc.) | Yes |
| Unwritten `use` DB | Absent from `_mdb_catalog.wt` | None (`0` `.wt` extents) | N/A (client-side pointer only) |

---

## 1.3 Database Destruction & Removal (db.dropDatabase())

> "db.dropDatabase() permanently deletes the currently selected database, including all of its collections and documents. This action cannot be undone."

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax (`db.dropDatabase()`) — Zero-Argument Context Binding & Wire Protocol.** In `mongosh`, `db.dropDatabase(writeConcern)` dispatches `{ dropDatabase: 1, writeConcern: ... }` against `db.getName()`. Passing a database name string inside `db.dropDatabase("schoolDB")` does **not** select `schoolDB`—any argument is interpreted as a `writeConcern` document, which is a classic operational hazard if the wrong database is active!
- **L-3.2 Operational Impact — Extent Unlinking, Oplog Replication & Irreversibility.** WiredTiger blocks concurrent operations on the target database via an exclusive database lock, unlinks all `collection-*.wt` and `index-*.wt` files in `O(C)` time (where `C` is collection count), immediately frees OS filesystem blocks, and writes a `{ op: "c", o: { dropDatabase: 1 } }` entry to the replication oplog.

```javascript
// Safe production teardown sequence in mongosh
use schoolDB
if (db.getName() === "schoolDB") {
  db.dropDatabase({ w: "majority" });
}
// Server executes { dropDatabase: 1, writeConcern: { w: "majority" } }
// Returns: { ok: 1, dropped: "schoolDB" }
// All .wt table and index extents are unlinked from the OS filesystem.
```

| Architectural Property | `db.dropDatabase()` Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| Underlying Wire Command | `{ dropDatabase: 1 }` |
| Locking Granularity | Exclusive database-level lock (`MODE_X`) |
| Disk Space Reclamation | Immediate OS filesystem block reclamation (unlinks `.wt` files) |
| Post-Drop Session Pointer | Session `db` variable still points to `schoolDB` (now unmaterialized) |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- **Architectural Invariant 1 — Deferred Extent Allocation**: `use <databaseName>` is a purely client-side lexical binding in `mongosh`; WiredTiger allocates `collection-*.wt` and `index-*.wt` files strictly upon the initial mutating write.
- **Architectural Invariant 2 — `{ listDatabases: 1 }` Catalog Scan**: `show dbs` queries `_mdb_catalog.wt` and computes `sizeOnDisk`; namespaces lacking persisted collections are filtered out.
- **Architectural Invariant 3 — Irreversible Extent Unlinking**: `db.dropDatabase()` acquires an exclusive database lock, purges all collections and B-tree indexes, and unlinks `.wt` extents directly from the OS filesystem without rollback.
